# Benchmarks

Kevlar vs [Polly v8](https://github.com/App-vNext/Polly) across every strategy, measured with [BenchmarkDotNet](https://benchmarkdotnet.org/) on GitHub Actions and republished automatically by the [benchmarks workflow](https://github.com/thomhurst/Kevlar/actions/workflows/benchmarks.yml).

*Last updated 2026-11-03 15:59 UTC (commit `c0dd3e3`).*

:::note
Microbenchmarks on shared CI runners are noisy. The **vs Polly** column is the median ratio over the most recent runs (up to 10); anything within ±20% is reported as *on par*. Absolute times move with runner hardware — the ratios are the signal.
:::

## Pipeline overhead floor

What an empty pipeline costs per execution — the fixed tax every strategy builds on.

| Scenario | Kevlar | Polly | Kevlar allocated | Polly allocated | Kevlar vs Polly |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Empty pipeline — async | 18.2 ns | 58.3 ns | 0 B | 0 B | **3.4× faster** |
| Empty pipeline — reference-state baseline | 14.6 ns | — | 0 B | — | — |
| Empty pipeline — caller-seeded context | 66.6 ns | — | 0 B | — | — |
| EmptyOutcomeState | 10.0 ns | — | 0 B | — | — |
| EmptyTaskOutcomeState | 12.5 ns | — | 0 B | — | — |
| Empty pipeline — zero-closure state overload | 17.7 ns | 62.6 ns | 0 B | 0 B | **3.6× faster** |
| Empty pipeline — sync | 9.6 ns | 29.3 ns | 0 B | 0 B | **3.5× faster** |
| NestedEmptyAsync | 103 ns | — | 0 B | — | — |
| NestedEmptySync | 94.5 ns | — | 0 B | — | — |
| NestedWithPropertiesAsync | 157 ns | — | 0 B | — | — |
| NestedWithPropertiesSync | 151 ns | — | 0 B | — | — |

## Retry

Happy path (judge overhead only) and a recovery path where every call fails twice before succeeding, with backoff disabled so only strategy machinery is measured.

| Scenario | Kevlar | Polly | Kevlar allocated | Polly allocated | Kevlar vs Polly |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Retry(3) — success on first attempt | 129 ns | 269 ns | 0 B | 24 B | **2.0× faster** |
| Retry(3) — two failures then success | 4.34 μs | 4.63 μs | 192 B | 328 B | on par |

## Timeout

The timeout never fires; this is the cost of arming and disarming the cancellation plumbing on every call.

| Scenario | Kevlar | Polly | Kevlar allocated | Polly allocated | Kevlar vs Polly |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Timeout(10 s) — completes instantly | 180 ns | 207 ns | 0 B | 0 B | **1.2× faster** |
| SynchronousGenerator_HappyPath | 218 ns | — | 0 B | — | — |
| AsynchronousGenerator_HappyPath | 1.69 μs | — | 560 B | — | — |
| AsyncHookConfigured_HappyPath | 210 ns | — | 0 B | — | — |

## Circuit breaker

Ratio/sampling bookkeeping while closed, and the fast-fail rejection cost while manually isolated — caught as a thrown exception, and read from the no-throw `ExecuteOutcomeAsync` API.

| Scenario | Kevlar | Polly | Kevlar allocated | Polly allocated | Kevlar vs Polly |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Isolated circuit — fast-fail rejection thrown | 5.56 μs | 5.50 μs | 1.3 KB | 1.3 KB | on par |
| Isolated circuit — fast-fail rejection via ExecuteOutcomeAsync | 107 ns | 187 ns | 144 B | 200 B | **1.7× faster** |
| Ratio breaker, closed — success | 177 ns | 262 ns | 0 B | 24 B | **1.5× faster** |
| DynamicDurationConfigured | 202 ns | — | 0 B | — | — |
| AsyncCallbackConfigured | 209 ns | — | 0 B | — | — |
| SlowCallDetectionConfigured | 304 ns | — | 0 B | — | — |

## Circuit breaker under contention

Eight workers share one open circuit, so every call is a fast-fail rejection observed as an outcome; this is the per-call cost during an outage.

| Scenario | Kevlar | Polly | Kevlar allocated | Polly allocated | Kevlar vs Polly |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Open circuit — 8 workers rejected | 64.5 ns | 196 ns | 144 B | 200 B | **3.2× faster** |

## Rate limit

Uncontended token-bucket permit acquisition — every call is admitted — and the rejection cost once the budget is exhausted, thrown vs `ExecuteOutcomeAsync`.

| Scenario | Kevlar | Polly | Kevlar allocated | Polly allocated | Kevlar vs Polly |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Budget exhausted — rejection thrown | 5.58 μs | 69.80 μs | 1.3 KB | 41.4 KB | **12× faster** |
| Budget exhausted — rejection via ExecuteOutcomeAsync | 162 ns | 46.90 μs | 136 B | 35.5 KB | **287× faster** |
| Token bucket — uncontended acquire | 152 ns | 156 ns | 0 B | 0 B | on par |
| WithHooks_Uncontended | 155 ns | — | 0 B | — | — |
| FrameworkAdapter_Uncontended | 154 ns | — | 0 B | — | — |
| PartitionedFrameworkAdapter_Uncontended | 190 ns | — | 32 B | — | — |

## Concurrency limit

A single caller against a large permit count; acquire/release cost with no queueing. The rejection rows hold the only permit and compare thrown vs `ExecuteOutcomeAsync`.

| Scenario | Kevlar | Polly | Kevlar allocated | Polly allocated | Kevlar vs Polly |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Permits exhausted — rejection thrown | 5.47 μs | 66.13 μs | 1.3 KB | 39.5 KB | **11× faster** |
| Permits exhausted — rejection via ExecuteOutcomeAsync | 101 ns | 42.82 μs | 136 B | 33.6 KB | **407× faster** |
| Concurrency limit — uncontended | 148 ns | 196 ns | 0 B | 40 B | **1.4× faster** |
| WithHooks_Uncontended | 154 ns | — | 0 B | — | — |
| Adaptive_Uncontended | 231 ns | — | 0 B | — | — |

## Typed result handling

Retry configured to treat a sentinel result as a failure; the returned value never matches, so this is the per-call cost of judging results.

| Scenario | Kevlar | Polly | Kevlar allocated | Polly allocated | Kevlar vs Polly |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Typed retry — result judged, no retry | 136 ns | 218 ns | 0 B | 0 B | **1.5× faster** |

## Composed pipelines

How per-call overhead scales with pipeline depth when nothing goes wrong.

| Scenario | Kevlar | Polly | Kevlar allocated | Polly allocated | Kevlar vs Polly |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Timeout → Retry → ratio breaker | 342 ns | 724 ns | 0 B | 48 B | **1.9× faster** |
| Token bucket → Timeout → Retry → ratio breaker → Concurrency limit | 507 ns | 947 ns | 0 B | 88 B | **2.0× faster** |
| TokenBucketRatioFiveStrategyChainSync | 468 ns | 1.02 μs | 0 B | 88 B | **2.2× faster** |

## Environment

- AMD EPYC 7763
- .NET 10.0.14 (10.0.14, 10.0.1426.52326), BenchmarkDotNet 0.15.8
- Times are medians; allocations are per operation.

## Reproduce

```bash
dotnet run -c Release --project benchmarks/Kevlar.Benchmarks -- --filter '*'
```

As always with microbenchmarks: measure your own workload before optimizing around these numbers. Nanosecond differences matter in tight loops and high-throughput services; they don't matter around a 50 ms network call.
